chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Musa al-Daq’qaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated that Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to me that Nasir ibn Ubayd narrated that Nasr ibn Mozahim al-Manqari narrated to me that Yahya ibn Ya'la, from Yahya ibn Salma ibn Kahil, from his father, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Abu Harb ibn Abi al-Aswad, from a man from Syria, from his father, who said: I heard the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) say:

"Among the worst of God's creation are five: Satan; the son of Adam who killed his brother; Pharaoh, Lord of the Stakes; a man from the Children of Israel who turned them away from their religion; and a man from this nation who pledges allegiance to disbelief at the gate of Ludd." He said: Then he said: "When I saw Muawiyah being pledged allegiance to at the gate of Ludd, I remembered the saying of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), so I joined Ali (peace be upon him) and remained with him."

key_terms.بَابِ لُدٍّ: Gate of Ludd (a city in Palestine)

ai.seo_question: Who are the five worst creatures of God according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq includes this narration in *Al-Khisal* to highlight the eschatological significance of Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, identifying him as the 'man from this Ummah' who pledged allegiance to disbelief at the gate of Ludd. This specific historical event served as the catalyst for the narrator's migration to join Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, illustrating the Shia scholarly emphasis on political allegiance as a marker of faith and the transition from the Prophet's era to the Imamate.
